subject: Offer exception: APAC (SG) COLA / onboarding stipend for GraceTech SRE hire
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Emily Park <emily.park@gracetech.com>, Jordan Bell <jordan.bell@talentpro.io>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Offer exception: APAC (SG) COLA / onboarding stipend for GraceTech SRE hire

Hi team,

Quick summary: GraceTech's candidate (Alex Turner) accepted verbally but needs a geo-specific onboarding + COLA adjustment to accept the offer formally. Candidate will be Singapore-based, remote. GraceTech is the hiring manager (Emily copied).

Current offer (standard IC3 SRE):
- Base: USD 145,000
- Equity: 0.30% 4yr
- Target comp band: IC3 US-equivalent
- Start date target: 2027-01-10

Request from hiring: add a Singapore-specific onboarding package and a small recurring COLA stipend to cover local market delta versus our US band. Hiring manager is requesting either:
A) One-time onboarding stipend: 10,000 SGD (grossed up) + one-month sign-on; or
B) Ongoing COLA stipend: 8,000 SGD/year (paid monthly) to keep take-home competitive.

Impacts I want us to sign off on before we send updated offer:
- Compensation band exception (if we bump base or make recurring stipend) — needs comp approval.
- Payroll / tax gross-up for the one-time amount if we want net-target.
- Budget / headcount allocation confirmation (GraceTech has headcount approved but this is an incremental comp hit).

Attachments: I started a quick payroll calc (payroll_onboarding_calc_SG.xlsx) with cost delta and simple gross-up scenarios. Also attached the current offer PDF for reference (GraceTech_offer_v1.pdf).

Ask: Laura — can you review and recommend whether A or B is preferable from comp and payroll standpoint?
Vivek — can you confirm hiring side willingness to pay the one-time vs recurring option (we should pick one for the candidate deadline: 2026-12-18)?
Maya / Marcus — loop in finance if you need a charge code.

Thanks — Olivia (Olga)

--
Olga Petrov
Head of Talent Partnerships (Contracting & Ops)
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 12:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Offer exception: APAC (SG) COLA / onboarding stipend for GraceTech SRE hire

Thanks for the context, Olga — reviewed the attached calc. A few notes: 

1) One-time onboarding stipend (10,000 SGD) 
   - If paid as a grossed-up, taxable payment run through payroll with gross-up, estimated employer cost ~ SGD 14k (see sheet). Payroll will need a gross-up template and a one-time tax adjustment.
   - Pros: cleaner for candidate, single admin event, easier to cap.
   - Cons: higher one-off cashflow (affects FY Q1 budgets).

2) Recurring COLA stipend (8,000 SGD/year)
   - If treated as an ongoing allowance it becomes part of payroll and increases benefits/taxable compensation; employer cost increases over time and impacts comp band comparators.
   - Pros: helps retention and maintains competitive take-home.
   - Cons: complicates comp benchmarking and band equity vs other IC3s.

Recommendation: approve option A (one-time grossed-up onboarding stipend) as a targeted exception. It minimizes ongoing comp compression risk and is simpler for total-cost forecasting. If hiring wants a keep incentive, add a 6-month retention clause (partial clawback if they leave within 6 months).

Comp exception: I can sign off on the one-time stipend up to 12,000 SGD grossed-up (comp exception note), provided Finance pre-approves the charge code. Please route to Marcus for charge code and to Vivek to confirm.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Total Rewards
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Emily Park <emily.park@gracetech.com>, Jordan Bell <jordan.bell@talentpro.io>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 07:41:00 +08:00
Subject: Re: Offer exception: APAC (SG) COLA / onboarding stipend for GraceTech SRE hire

Thanks — agree with Laura's recommendation. GraceTech is comfortable with option A (one-time onboarding grossed-up payment). Key points from hiring:
- Offer should keep base at the US-equivalent band (USD 145k) and not elevate base band.
- Approve a one-time onboarding stipend up to 12,000 SGD grossed-up with a 6-month pro-rata clawback if voluntary departure.
- Start date target still 2027-01-10; please expedite updated offer and DocuSign.

Olga — please prepare updated offer (include grossed-up stipend language and clawback clause). Marcus — can you confirm finance charge code and that we can absorb FY Q1 cashflow?

Vivek
VP, Infrastructure Engineering
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: Offer exception: APAC (SG) COLA / onboarding stipend for GraceTech SRE hire

Forwarding on behalf of candidate — Alex confirmed today that the one-time onboarding payment (grossed-up) is acceptable and will sign as soon as DocuSign is live. He also asked for a short note on tax handling so his Singapore advisor can prepare (per Laura, it's payrolled and grossed-up).

Alex's note (forwarded):
> Hi all — thanks. I appreciate the one-time stipend option. If we can get the DocuSign by end of day tomorrow I can return signed and target the Jan 10 start. Quick ask: can payroll include a line item description in the offer so my tax advisor has visibility?

Olga — can you confirm you'll include the payroll language and push the DocuSign link? Emily — candidate is eager; hiring team ready.

-Jordan
